proof_summary: For $p\equiv3\pmod4$, splitting the nonzero residues into squares and negatives and evaluating quadratic character sums yields matrix identities that turn the determinant, after a column permutation, into that of $S-S^{T}Z$; here $S$ is invertible and normal and $Z$ is a determinant-one symmetric involution, so odd-dimensional orthogonality forces singularity. For $p\equiv1\pmod4$, reduction modulo $p$, Wilson’s theorem, binomial expansion, and Vandermonde moment arguments show that any kernel vector must vanish, proving nonsingularity modulo $p$ and hence nonvanishing of the integer determinant.
